Debates and Scholars: Who Argues What

Reminder (Methodology §1.4): a debater "winning" a stage event is rhetoric, not evidence. This chapter maps which arguments belong to whom so the reader can trace claims to their sources, not crown winners.

1. Neutral / academic scholarship (the arbiter's baseline)

ScholarFieldCore relevant contribution
Bart D. EhrmanNT textual criticismVariants & "orthodox corruptions"; concedes no core doctrine rests on a disputed text. Also skeptical of traditional Qur'an origins.
Bruce MetzgerNT textual criticismStandard methodology; the early text is reconstructable.
Larry Hurtado / Richard BauckhamChristian originsVery early high Christology within Jewish monotheism.
Daniel B. WallaceNT manuscriptsManuscript abundance → high recoverability (Christian scholar, academically rigorous).
François Déroche / Behnam Sadeghi / Asma HilaliQur'anic manuscriptsSanaa palimpsest; early ʿUthmanic standardization with pre-standard variation.
Nicolai Sinai / Angelika Neuwirth / Gabriel S. Reynolds / Sean AnthonyQur'anic studiesQur'an as a datable late-antique text; literary & historical analysis.
John Wansbrough / Patricia Crone / Michael CookRevisionist originsLate-canonization thesis — largely undercut by early manuscript dating; now minority.
Keith SmallComparative MS criticism"Preservation by elimination" (Qur'an) vs. "by comparison" (NT).

These are the voices an arbiter weights most, because they argue from physical and textual data and publish under peer review.

2. Christian apologetic debaters

FigureSignature arguments
William Lane CraigPhilosophical defense of God + Trinity coherence; historical case for the resurrection.
James WhiteManuscript abundance; defense against Islamic tahrif; qiraʾat & Sanaa used in reverse.
Mike Licona / Gary Habermas"Minimal facts" historical argument for the resurrection.
Jay SmithAggressive use of Sanaa/Birmingham/qiraʾat against Qur'anic perfect-preservation claims.
Nabeel Qureshi (d. 2017)Narrative/experiential + historical-Jesus case.

Recurring Christian move: concede NT variants, then argue recoverability + early high Christology, then turn the corruption standard back onto the Qur'an (symmetry).

3. Muslim apologetic debaters

FigureSignature arguments
Ahmed Deedat (d. 2005)Pioneered the popular Bible-contradictions / tahrif style.

Shabir AllyThe most academically engaged; uses Ehrman & critical NT scholarship carefully.

Recurring Muslim move: deploy Ehrman + the disputed passages for tahrif, and press the *logical simplicity of tawhid*** against the Trinity.

4. Honest concessions on each side (signal vs. noise)

A useful filter: weight arguments that the other side's own experts concede.

  • Conceded toward the Muslim case: the NT is not letter-perfect; Comma Johanneum, Mark 16:9–20, John 7:53–8:11 are not original; the Trinity is post-biblical in formulation. (Conceded by mainstream Christian scholarship.)
  • Conceded toward the Christian case: the Qur'an's text was unified by destroying variant codices; the Sanaa lower text and the *canonical qiraʾat are real internal variation; the strong revisionist "very late Qur'an" thesis is weak. (Conceded or demonstrated by mainstream Qur'anic scholarship; some, like Qadhi, say so publicly.)*

The genuinely strong, defensible claims are exactly the ones the opposing experts do not dispute. Everything that only one camp's debaters assert should be treated as contested until traced to the data in chapters 02–05.
